question.text: Sodium fusion extract of an organic compound gives a blood red colouration with few drops of <math> <mrow>  <msub>   <mrow>    <mtext>FeCl</mtext></mrow>   <mtext>3</mtext>  </msub>  </mrow></math> solution. This indicates the presence of

options.text: Nitrogen and sulphur in the organic compound
Sulphur and chlorine in the organic compound

solution.text: The presence of both nitrogen and sulphur in the lassaigne's test in an organic compound shows a blood red colouration with  <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">F</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">l</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></math>  solution. This is due to the formation of NaCNS in the sodium fusion extract.
